topic: F-V01-13 exact loaded Ubuntu SQLite WAL-reset classification

fresh_external_primary_evidence.finding: The WAL-reset race is likely present in upstream versions 3.7.0 through 3.51.2 and fixed in 3.51.3+, with selected backports.
Exact source package sqlite3_3.45.1-1ubuntu2.7 is available; component SHA256 values were verified from its .dsc during target execution.

question: Did Ubuntu backport or equivalently fix the WAL-reset defect in the exact libsqlite3-0 3.45.1-1ubuntu2.7 object currently loaded by Frank's accepted Ubuntu target, making the private 3.53.4 lane unnecessary?

hypothesis.claim: The currently loaded Ubuntu 3.45.1-1ubuntu2.7 SQLite remains vulnerable to the targeted WAL-reset defect because its exact downstream source lineage lacks an equivalent fix.

strongest_counterhypothesis.claim: Canonical backported or independently implemented an equivalent fix while retaining the 3.45.1 version surface, so the loaded object will survive the deterministic upstream regression sequence.

target_execution.workflow: SQLite Ubuntu loaded-runtime Axis D v2

targeted_fault_result.fault_hook_scope: test-only deterministic upstream-derived hook at WAL checkpoint copy path

falsification_adjudication.limits: Deterministic fault regression proves susceptibility of the exact source lineage to the documented failure mode; it does not quantify natural occurrence rate or power-loss behavior.

architecture_delta.name: DO_NOT_USE_CURRENT_SYSTEM_SQLITE_FOR_CORRECTNESS_SENSITIVE_MULTI_CONNECTION_WAL_STATE
architecture_delta.decision: The current target system SQLite cannot remain the accepted runtime for correctness-sensitive multi-connection WAL state. Integrate an explicitly bound fixed runtime; the separately target-green private SQLite 3.53.4 candidate from PR #315 is the current measured candidate because it passes the same targeted defect discriminator and the process-crash oracle.
architecture_delta.successor_gate: Production Frank processes must prove at runtime which SQLite object/source id they loaded, prove it belongs to a fixed accepted lineage, rerun state/effect/presence differential gates on that exact bound runtime, and retain rollback/fail-closed behavior.

instrument_negative_result.repair: Axis-D v2 removed unsupported configure flag and bound unmodified source id before test instrumentation.

next_frontier: Compose the already target-green private SQLite 3.53.4 candidate into an explicit Frank storage runtime boundary without replacing the host system package.
Re-run presence, V17 re-entry/DONE, GWT causal support and crash/restart suites under the exact selected fixed SQLite object.
Add runtime source-id/object-hash admission so accidental fallback to vulnerable system SQLite fails closed.
Keep power-loss/kernel-panic durability as a separate unresolved gate.
go_oob_experiment: NONE_IN_CYCLE_4; the macrocycle's single OOB slot was already consumed in cycle 1
